items.title: Kenny Davern interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clearwater Beach, Florida, March 16, 2001 [interview 2 of 2]

ctx.x: Yeah. We just used to hang around there looking at — you’d see Benny Goodman rehearsing, you’d see Artie Shaw rehearsing, you’d see Tommy Dorsey rehearsing. And there was Shep Fields rehearsing. Well I said what harm could this do? And there was a sign out there, we need a baritone sax and bass clarinet players, so fine, boom, I sat down in the chair and played. Oh good, what’s your name kid? And that’s how I got with Ralph Flanagan. I finally graduated high school and then they held the auditions, and word got…

Thompson?” He said, “Yes I am.” I said, “My name is Kenny Davern and I can’t wait this line, you see I have a gig” — which I was lying through my teeth — “I have to be at a gig in about 45 minutes and I wonder if it would be possible for me to—” He said, “Okay.” And he took me in. Well there in back of the screen was Ralph Flanagan putzing around on the piano and a bass player and a drummer. And he puts up the sheet music and I take out my horn.
